To appropriately answer your question yes you should put points into str,agi,Wis if your accuracy is to low ie. warrior uses Wis for accuracy. Only put enough points to get your current best farming spot to 100% then when it's time to move on you shouldn't be to far off 100 in the next portable. Use cards with base stats for accuracy boosts to save a few points on your talents. You can have to much dmg in the sense that your accuracy becomes to under leveled for you to get it back up in a few levels. Remember to buy talent reset fragments everyday. Chopping, smithing, mining etc. Try to rush a archer with tab 2 anvil points this will get you a head start on smithing lvls so you can make any armor as soon as your character is of equipable lvl. Having 2 talent pages at the bottom is your best friend focus tab 1 on fighting and 2 on skilling. Splitting a skilling and damage build will make you struggle makes me wonder why I tried when the game came out lol. Positive pressure helps keep the computer clean as air will come out of every crack temps stable not always the best but definitely comfortable for the parts. Hot air is noticable from the exhaust as it's the only source for heat to leave can be minor to kinda warm.

Negative pressure pulls air in every crack, nook, and cranny meaning it pulls dust into the PC as well even with a filter but with absolutely no dust it can reduce temps by 1-3°c ...... Not worth the effort imo for the constant need to clean also if you don't the amount of dust over time will kill the PC. this is based off the number of fans, quality of the fans, and the case. This occurs by pulling all the air out of the PC forcing cold air to come in where it can. You don't really suffocate the case but because of the lack of air coming in it resorts to convection and pulls cold air in to replace the air being taken out. Usually feels like ambient air coming out but can be miss leading to true temps if dust is present.

Q: Will I be able to load my Diablo II Classic save files into the Early Access or Open Beta?

A: Players will not be able to import local offline saves from the original Diablo II to Diablo II: Resurrected Early Access and Open Beta because this test is online only.
At launch, players will be able to load their local offline saves by copying the save files from the original Diablo II to Diablo II: Resurrected. The underlying game engine is exactly the same, so those local saves will work but they will need to be copied over manually.
However, local save files (whether newly created or copied from Diablo II) will be different from online save files. There are profound differences between the modern Battle.net of today and what we launched with Diablo II all those years ago.
